methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia Tech adopts universitywide human-centered AI vision | ETIH EdTech News - EdTech Innovation Hub
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's universitywide human-centered AI vision signals institutional capability-building that could radiate through Southwest Virginia via student diffusion and regional partnerships, potentially counteracting NoVA concentration if implementation extends beyond campus.

signals.title: Roanoke College partners with Google for free AI training - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Google's free AI training partnership with Roanoke College represents platform-delivered shallow distribution—offering broad access without deep technical capability development, fitting the 'Software Does It For You' pathway in a traditionally underserved region.

signals.title: Left hand, right hand: Virginia cools on data centers even as state policy promotes the AI that requires them - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's contradictory stance—promoting AI policy while cooling on data centers—reveals a disconnect between concentrated infrastructure development (primarily NoVA) and distributed economic benefit, reinforcing rather than bridging regional capability gaps.

signals.title: Virginia Tech Researchers Use AI to Gauge Manufacturing Water Needs - GovTech
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech researchers applying AI to manufacturing water needs demonstrates deep technical capability being developed for practical industrial applications, with potential to distribute expertise to Shenandoah Valley and Southside manufacturing communities if knowledge transfer occurs.

signals.title: How one Virginia county’s AI platform protects sensitive data - Route Fifty
signals.signal_reading: A Virginia county developing its own AI platform with data protection capabilities signals emerging deep technical competency at the local government level, suggesting distributed capability-building beyond traditional tech hubs if other localities can replicate this approach.
